comments.body_html:
I was facing a similar issue but once I realized the zipped folder wasn’t extracting the way it should, I tried doing it manually and that worked.

What you should do is try downloading the zipped folder to another folder that isn’t your root SPT-AKI install folder (example, an “SPT-AKI Mods” folder). Extract the SPT-VR folder with 7-Zip using the “extract here” method. You should end up with a folder called SPT-VR. Inside that folder are two other folders, BepInEx and EscapeFromTarkov_Data. These two folders already exist in your SPT-AKI root folder. Copy+paste one folder at a time form the SPT-VR folder to your SPT-AKI root folder. Verify that the contents of the SPT-VR folder made it into the respective SPT-AKI folders by opening them up and checking that the contents from the original extracted SPT-VR folder now exist in the SPT-AKI BepInEx and EscapeFromTarkov_Data folders.

I know that’s a long explanation, but I wanted to be certain you know what to do from start to finish. It’s a pretty incredible project and everyone should try it out.

After hours of testing configs and mods, I finally started playing for real and want to share some tips for anyone trying this mod.

First of all, aiming in Tarkov VR is tough. Whether you’re using iron sights or a 12x scope, it’s significantly harder than other VR shooters. I strongly recommend always using a laser or, at minimum, a 1x scope.

I searched for mods to disable weapon sway, and the only one I found was SPT Realism. I ended up disabling most of the mod’s features and turning off the sway entirely.

Note to CYBENSIS: Please add a sway option to the mod—my shaky hands provide enough sway on their own! 😆

Second, there’s the bot difficulty. I could barely win any fights; either the AI was sniping me from super far away, or their reaction time was too fast to keep up with in VR. To make things more balanced, I installed the SAIN mod, selected Baby Bots, and made a few tweaks.

After all that, I ended up playing for five hours straight! My feet are killing me, but wow, what an experience. Thanks again for the mod!

It depends on your headset and the resolution you set per eye. For example, on my Pico 4, I use a 4000x4000 resolution with a 400 Mbps bitrate. I also use FSR, which downscales and then upscales the image. This causes some quality loss but lets me maintain the same FPS as if I set it to 2000x2000.

comments.author: Disya123
comments.body_html:
Check the vr resolution in steam, you should have it at least 2000x2000.

Also if you have enabled program ovr dynamic revolution, set its static resolution mode to 100%

Don’t forget about the recommendations from the developer.

In-game graphics guide

  • Resolution likely doesn’t matter much as it’s always going to render to the quality of your headset or what SteamVR is set to, but lowering the resolution may net some frames.
  • Anti-aliasing should be off or on FXAA - No FPS difference noticed between the two, and other options cause visual glitches.
  • Resampling should be off/1x, otherwise it may cause visual glitches.
  • DLSS and FSR don’t work properly, so turn them both off.
  • HBAO - Looks better but takes a massive hit on performance - off gets about a 10-20 FPS increase.
  • SSR - Low drops frames by around 2-5, ultra by about 5ish. I don’t personally notice any visual improvements but if you have it on, go to ultra.
  • Anisotropic filtering - No real FPS difference.
  • Sharpness at 1-1.5 - Any visual gain falls off after around 1.5+.
  • POST FX - Turning it off gains about 8-10 FPS in some situations, or does nothing in others.

Guys I just realized I forgot to come back to this, sorry.

I actually got my graphics looking 100% times better, I did a combination of 2 things - 1 of which will only be applicable to Quest users.

Firstly, I changed some settings in the Quest 2 Debug tool which is typically stored here:

C:\Program Files\Oculus\Support\oculus-diagnostics

The settings I changed here were:

  • Set Encode Resolution Width: 4096
  • Set Bitrate: 200 Mbps (onlyrequired if using Link or Air Link)
  • Set Distortion Curvature to Low.
  • Set Encode Dynamic Bitrate to Disabled.

Secondly, I cranked up the SteamVR resolution to super sample the image:

  • Open SteamVR > Settings > Video
  • Set Render Resolution to something between 150%–200%, depending on what your PC can run.

Lastly, to get some extra FPS back, I did the below:

I set the display resolution in the game’s settings to be as low as possible - this helped heaps as my monitor is 1440p ultrawide and it was really taxing my performance having it render on the 1440p screen .

If you have a similar setup, you could probably switch the window the game opens on to be your secondary 1080p 24 in side monitor.

It all still ran quite well on my PC which has the below specs:

  • 5800x3d
  • 4070 TI, non OC or tuned.
  • 24gb RAM (1 dead RAM slot :’[ )

Doing all of this improved the graphics quality significantly. It’s still not quite perfect in SPT VR, but its been a major improvement - and not only for SPT VR, but for all Quest VR games look so much better. I am really satisfied with the graphics on my Quest 2 now, I was almost considering upgrading, but I can get much more use out of it for now.

comments.author: matsix
comments.body_html:
I actually took a really hard look into this when I took it over because I’m also an index user and yeah the flickering is really annoying. I don’t think I’ll be able to do much about it though.

Basically, what’s mainly causing it to look really bad is something called specular aliasing, it happens from specularity on materials in the game world, so like glossiness. The problem is that Tarkov uses deferred rendering which doesn’t support MSAA which is the best AA solution for VR by far. The only other options in deferred rendering which actually help with specular aliasing is DLSS, FSR3, or TAA. All of which doesn’t work in SPTVR because well, DLSS specifically for VR isn’t really supported in Unity (it is in Unreal). Also, the postprocesslayer needs to be disabled for VR otherwise things don’t work right (same image in both eyes) and I think that actually needs to be enabled for TAA, FSR3, or DLSS to work. I know it for sure is needed for TAA.

I’ll take a look at it again at some point but for now the best option is using something like Reshade to handle some anti aliasing, it doesn’t do great and doesn’t help with specular aliasing but helps a bit with other aliasing. And mixing Reshade with VRperfkit which uses FSR1, also doesn’t help much with specular aliasing but it does at least a bit.

There is something called geometric specular anti aliasing (gsaa) which might help if I can figure out how to force it onto all materials somehow.

SteamVR has had an update as of 5/6/2025. Which caused Reshade to break a lot of VR games. Reshade has released an update 5/29/2025 which fixes it, download the latest version if you use Reshade.

Install VRAMCleaner - VRAM Cleaner

Latest update grenade guide:

  • Pull grenade out, same way you always would from quickslot radial menu
  • Hold trigger to pull pin
  • Yeet the grenade by letting go of trigger as you do the throwing motion

You can throw grenades hard, light, under hand them, chuck them hard like a baseball, lob them high, anything. Works like a native VR game.

Will this be updated for SPT 4.0?

It already has been, it’ll be available once SPT 4.0 goes live.

Performance Guide!

So, there’s a lot of people that think this mod is impossible to play and actually have decent performance. That is not true unless you’re going to streets of course which runs horrible even on flatscreen. So here’s what I suggest to get the best performance as someone that has been using this mod since before it released publicly.

First off, SPTVR is best played with a direct wired connection to your PC. If you use a quest or some other headset and are trying to do wireless streaming, you will not have a good time with VRAM usage. If you have a card with a lot of VRAM, go for it, if not, then you absolutely need a wired connection.

For reference my specs -

RTX 3080 10GB

32GB of ram

Ryzen 5 7600x

NVME SSD

  1. Install VRAMCleaner - VRAM Cleaner
  2. Set all graphics settings to lowest/off except textures, shadows, anisotropic, and LOD/visibility (set those to whatever you want) AA should always be set to FXAA, nothing else works
  3. Check boxes on graphics settings at bottom, Grass shadows, high quality color, and streets low quality textures. Everything else unchecked, volumetric lighting is your preference
  4. Install VRPerfKit - https://github.com/RavenSystem/VRPerfKit_RSF/releases (may not be needed when using VRAMCleaner)
  5. (Skip if not using VRPerfkit) Open the .yml file in notepad for perfkit and change renderscale to like 30
  6. (Skip if not using VRPerfkit) In SteamVR settings set resolution for tarkov to something really high, I set mine to about 400% with my valve index (this step and 4 can be adjusted based on the VRAM you have available on your graphics card and which headset you use, you may be able to go higher, my graphics card only has 10GB of VRAM)
  7. Learn how to use a headless fika client, there’s videos and guides online (this is the biggest improvement you can get in performance) even running the headless on your own PC will be a pretty good help, if you do run it on your own PC, you should have at minimum 32GB of RAM
  8. Install a bot spawner mod such as MOAR or ABPS, these are also big helps to performance because the main killer of performance in SPT is the AI. These mods are much better at managing spawns.
  9. Last thing I’d suggest which may not apply for many people, I disable my 4k monitor whenever I play which seems to help a bit.

For everbody struggling with the extreme aliasing, that’s what helped me to make it more bearable:

1. Switching off hbao and ssr. On sunny weather they massively increased the aliasing ladders

5. Oculus debug tool -> distortion curvature low, link sharpening off. High distortion curvature makes the image worce at the outer half of your fov, link sharpening, well, it sharpens the already oversharpened image

P.s. note for the developer: I’ve noticed that in default settings (which give a bad image), the picture inside the optical scope is actually pretty good and doesn’t have ladders at all. comments.author: matsix
comments.body_html:
It’s not really a unity problem, it’s just a VR problem in general. Most VR games use forward rendering rather than deferred rendering so that they can use MSAA which is the best for VR. Unfortunately, you can’t really just change a games whole render pipeline to forward if it’s been built with deferred.

The problem with not being able to use Post Processing for TAA/DLSS/FSR is actually a BSG thing. I think they’ve customized unity’s post processing so much to the point where VR just doesn’t work with it. Unity’s post processing is actually supposed to be compatible with VR. I recently tried my hand again at getting post processing working so that we can get those upscalers working but had no luck.

comments.author: matsix
comments.body_html:
Pretty big progress update on 1.1.3

  • Various optimizations
  • Adjusted ramp for hold breath smoothing, the smoothing should ramp up more now the higher your zoom is
  • Shoulder positioning 2.0 - Shoulders are now placed nearly perfectly, you will be able to aim up now without your left arm pulling back and detaching from the gun foregrip. This also just feels like an overall improvement for the arm IK
  • Toggles in VR settings to disable frustum and occlusion culling GPUInstancing, unfortunately couldn’t figure out a way to get it working properly for multipass stereo so just added toggles. This completely resolves the issue of grass culling all the way to the right in your right eye and also grass disappearing in your right eye when a gun is blocking it in your left eye. If you’re worried about performance, you can disable occlusion culling and leave frustum on. Occlusion culls out grass behind gun, frustum culls out the grass on the right
  • Auto arm length adjustment when loading into a raid and when using the reset height bind - this isn’t perfect I currently have this working by moving your shoulders forward/backward based on your height. So I had to sort of hold it back a bit to avoid your shoulders moving too much and causing IK issues
  • Quick transfer items to sell at trader by holding right grip and pressing A
  • Quick reload added, works by double tapping the reload button
  • Update to head to leg sync, when looking down while walking, legs will not move ahead of your head position anymore, same for looking up, legs won’t move back further when looking up while walking
  • Reduced timer on when movement stop is detected, before when you would stop and then try leaning, your legs will follow too quickly. There was a delay between moving and stopping, I reduced that timer. So now as soon as you stop moving and try leaning, legs shouldn’t instantly follow. Together with the previous point, this makes leaning a lot more predictable

And more coming, I really want this to be the best extraction shooter experience for VR. The amount of custom work being done to completely alter Tarkov to work for VR is just insane. I know if people look at my code, they may think I have no idea what I’m doing. Well, they would be right. This project is being driven by sheer will and love for VR alone. I might be doing some total non-sense but if it means making the experience better in VR then that’s all that matters to me.

comments.body_html:
Note of transparency:

So, I just want to be completely transparent when it comes to this project. Since I’ve taken over on this project, I wouldn’t deny, I’ve used AI quite a bit to help me along but always used it in a way where it helped me more than worked for me, I always used ILSpy/dnspy to analyze everything manually and had it help with making sense of some things. Unfortunately, I started hitting a ceiling and things started stressing me out more instead of just enjoying the process, things like manual interactions seemed so far out of reach which sucks because I love this project so much and want it to be the best it can be. I want people to feel like they’re in the world of Tarkov.

With that, the part I want to be transparent about. Starting from next update, I’m going to start leaning on AI a lot more. I will always review code to make sure I understand how it’s working and that it’s not doing anything bad (I know the rules on AI usage, if any SPT moderators wants to make sure I understand the code, just shoot me a dm). I’d be an idiot to deny using a tool that has proved itself to be incredibly useful. It’s like working on something that requires a wrench, that wrench being right next to you, and refusing to use it. Since connecting my project to Claude and letting it help with decompiling and understanding how the game works, I have fixed some huge issues that have been long time issues in the mod.

Finally - it helped me get started on the first implementations of manual interactions.

So, while some people may not like this shift, I hope the next update helps to show why I decided to do this.

Next update is going straight to version 1.3.0 - Full food/drink manual interactions is coming :) That marks the start of the roadmap to manual reloads! I’ll be slowly adding more manual interactions each update. The goal is to make most of the game entirely interactive in VR, as in, little to no UI needed while in a raid.
